subject: Post-demo: end-to-end latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: end-to-end latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Jonathan — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed qualification plan so we can align on expectations before running an apples-to-apples test between your current provider and Redwood hosted API.

Summary from the call:
- Target end-to-end p95: 120 ms
- Target end-to-end p99: 400 ms
- Peak sustained concurrency: 200 concurrent requests (burst to 600 for short windows)
- Streaming usage: client uses chunked streaming for long responses (~2–3 KB per chunk); ~15% of calls use streaming
- Payloads: average request size ~1.1 KB, occasional large prompts (<= 12 KB)
- SLA/observability requirements: request-level traces and token-level timing for debugging

What we need from Acme to run the hosted evaluation:
1) Sample production request traces (headers, round-trip timings) — attach as JSON if possible (we referenced this on the call).
2) Representative dataset of prompts (50–100) and expected response-length distribution.
3) Traffic profile: RPS distribution over 24h and a 10-minute peak snapshot.
4) Target model(s) you want validated (name + params + quantization if known).
5) A short test window you can approve (we normally run a 72-hour window with two 4-hour focused load windows).

Redwood proposed test plan (high level):
- Measurement definition: end-to-end = client->Redwood API endpoint -> model inference -> response fully received by client. We'll include client-side latency (so we match your in-prod instrumentation).
- Synthetic harness: Rishi will run a replay harness that replays your traces at scale (100% fidelity for timing/arrival patterns).
- Streaming validation: replicate chunking behavior for streaming calls to check memory and backpressure characteristics.
- Data handling: traces/prompt corpus will be used only for performance qualification and deleted after the test; we can sign an NDA if helpful.

Attachments: slo_requirements_matrix.xlsx (filled with the targets above).

Next steps / asks (owners):
- Jonathan: share sample traces + prompt corpus + preferred test window (by EOD tomorrow)
- Rishi (cc): will prepare the harness and a preliminary config for your review
- Vivek (cc): will validate network egress options for the test and confirm regional routing
- Neha: I’ll coordinate schedule and share the test acceptance criteria doc once we agree

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync early next week to confirm the test window and sign off on the acceptance criteria?

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

From: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@acmerobotics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T12:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: end-to-end latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Neha — appreciate the recap and clear plan. A few clarifications and I attached the initial traces.

Clarifications from our side:
- Our p95/p99 targets are measured at the gateway (client → gateway) which includes our lightweight preprocessing layer. We’ll share instrumentation notes so you can match that boundary.
- Concurrency: the 200 concurrent number reflects sustained worker-concurrency; our front-end will cap active connections to 1,000 during bursts but upstream workers smooth it down.
- For streaming: chunk sizes vary but the path you described matches production behavior.

Attachments included: acme_trace_samples.json (sanitized traces), prompt_corpus_sample.txt (30 prompts). We also pasted a short RPS profile in the attachment metadata. We prefer the 72-hour window with two focused 4-hour load windows — Oct 13–15 works for us.

Two asks for Redwood:
1) Can you include p95/p99 reported both at the client-observed boundary and at the model-inference boundary (so we can separate network vs model time)?
2) We will need an exec summary (1 page) within 48 hours of test completion for our procurement team.

I’m ok with an NDA for the traces — our legal team prefers you use our standard mutual NDA (I can loop them in if needed).

Thanks,
Jonathan Price
Dir. of Platform Engineering, Acme Robotics
jonathan.price@acmerobotics.com | +1 617-555-0132

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: end-to-end latency qualification & next steps (hosted vs current provider)

Jonathan — perfect, thanks for the traces and the preferred window. Quick confirmation and plan update: 

Measurement breakdown we will deliver (by metric):
- Client-observed p95/p99: measured at the same ingress boundary you provided in traces (we will run a client-side agent).
- Model-inference p95/p99: latency inside the model execution path (time spent after request deserialized to model output ready).
- End-to-end delta: we will surface both absolute numbers and the contribution breakdown (network, preprocessing, queuing, inference, serialization).

Test execution plan (owners & timeline):
- Today: Rishi will validate harness fits your trace format and share the harness config (redwood_test_plan.md attached).
- Oct 9–12: small smoke runs to validate fidelity and streaming chunking behavior (non-contentious tests; low risk).
- Oct 13–15: full 72-hour run with two 4-hour focused load windows (we will run both your current provider and Redwood hosted in separate controlled windows).
- Within 48 hours of test completion: Redwood will provide a 1-page exec summary plus a full measurement report (CSV + graphs) and raw anonymized samples.

Network & security notes: Vivek will send a short checklist of egress IPs and required firewall rules — please apply for the test window. We will accept your mutual NDA; Jonathan, if you can DM the legal contact we’ll get that signed ASAP.

Action items (owners):
- Jonathan: share legal contact for NDA, confirm firewall change owner, and approve Oct 13–15 window (blocked)
- Rishi: finalize harness config and run smoke tests (owner: rishi@redwood.com)
- Vivek: firewall/egress checklist & routing confirmation (owner: vivek@redwood.com)
- Neha: schedule follow-up 30-min sync post-run to walk procurement through the 1-pager

I'll set the follow-up calendar invite once NDA is in place. Thanks again — looking forward to getting a clean comparison that separates network and model contributions.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187
